questions.answer:
The Euclidean norm is the square root of the sum of squared components:
\[
\|\mathbf v\|=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}.
\]
Compute:
\[
\|\mathbf v\|=\sqrt{9+16}=\sqrt{25}=5.
\]
So \(\|\mathbf v\|=5\).

Distance is the norm of the difference vector. First compute
\[
Q-P=(4-1,2-(-2),-1-3)=(3,4,-4).
\]
Now take the norm:
\[
d(P,Q)=\sqrt{3^2+4^2+(-4)^2}.
\]
Thus
\[
d(P,Q)=\sqrt{9+16+16}=\sqrt{41}.
\]
The distance is \(\sqrt{41}\).

questions.prompt: Let \(\mathbf v=(2,-1,2)\). Find a unit vector in the same direction as \(\mathbf v\).
questions.answer:
A unit vector in the same direction is \(\mathbf v/\|\mathbf v\|\). First compute the norm:
\[
\|\mathbf v\|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+2^2}=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3.
\]
Divide each component by \(3\):
\[
\frac{\mathbf v}{\|\mathbf v\|}=\frac{1}{3}(2,-1,2)=\left(\frac23,-\frac13,\frac23\right).
\]
This vector has norm \(1\) and points in the same direction as \(\mathbf v\).

Use the Euclidean norm formula:
\[
\|(t,2)\|=\sqrt{\(t^2\)+2^2}=5.
\]
Square both sides:
\[
\(t^2\)+4=25.
\]
Subtract \(4\):
\[
\(t^2\)=21.
\]
Therefore
\[
t=\pm\sqrt{21}.
\]
Both values work because the norm uses \(t^2\).
